blocks.text:
Day 4 · Full-day excursion to Torres del Paine National Park, one of the great natural highlights of Patagonia. The day begins at the Milodón Cave on Cerro Benítez, about 25 km from Puerto Natales, where the remains of several prehistoric animals, including the giant ground sloth known as the mylodon, were discovered in 1895. Spend around 30 minutes exploring the cave, its stalactite formations and a replica of the mylodon.

In the park, the landscape changes from Magellanic forest to vast Patagonian plains framed by rugged mountains, glaciers, rivers and crystal-clear lakes. A short 15-minute walk leads to Salto Grande, the waterfall linking Lake Nordenskjöld and Lake Pehoé; the scenic route then passes the Serrano River and Lakes Toro and Porteño before returning to the hotel.

Above the Patagonian steppe rise the park’s iconic granite towers. Part of UNESCO’s network of Biosphere Reserves since 1978, Torres del Paine is home to rheas (ñandú), Andean condors, flamingos and guanacos, whose thriving herds are one of the park’s great conservation success stories.
